captureNotes: Real TaskWindow captures of the running app on a separate local database with fictional data (The Harbour Cafe). The dark capture activates the app's own prefers-color-scheme rule through CSSOM; no UI content is substituted. Desktop capture is a 1440x960 emulated viewport.

screenshots.title: The published week
screenshots.alt: A Monday-to-Sunday shift grid with people down the side, an open-shifts row, and conflict warnings drawn on the cells that cause them.

screenshots.alt: The same Monday-to-Sunday shift grid in the app's dark theme.

cover.title: OpenShifts
cover.subtitle: Scheduling, time tracking and shift swaps for teams that work shifts.
cover.headline:
A published week
is a promise.

features.title:
A published week
is a promise.
features.subtitle: Publish the week. Every change after that is recorded, with who made it and how much notice people got.
features.alt: Conceptual floating week ready to publish, with a slightly overlapping panel listing a change made after publishing and the notice it carried.

features.title:
Caught before
it goes out.
features.subtitle: Stated availability, approved leave, double bookings and short rest are checked as you assign, not after.
features.alt: Conceptual floating shift assignment showing an availability conflict, with an overlapping panel of what that person said they could not work.

features.title:
Every swap
leaves a trail.
features.subtitle: Who gave the shift up, who took it, and who said yes. A decision with a name and a time on it.
features.alt: Conceptual floating shift swap awaiting approval, with an overlapping panel showing when it was offered up and when it was claimed.

features.title:
Know the wage bill
before you commit.
features.subtitle: Hours and cost for the week against the budget you set, with overtime past your own threshold.
features.alt: Conceptual floating weekly wage total against a budget with a per-person breakdown, and an overlapping panel showing the overtime rule.
